Upstream reports complete section/ending QA and v1.2 software regression passes. Physical MiSTer and flash-cart confirmation remains outstanding, and heavy scenes still drop frames. Current release notes describe local builds rather than a GitHub release or a confirmed itch upload.

title: Softporn Adventure — SC-3000 native C port
reason: Native C parser/game state, console and adventure implementation accompanies retained Pascal source. Pascal header explicitly distinguishes CP/M and IBM PC screen layout; C recreates its command dispatch. SDCC/SGlib build creates an SC cartridge. Release 0.60 provides a 48 KiB ROM and gameplay fixes; 0.50 is explicitly called playable upstream. Historical adult-themed adventure. Readme is empty and original Apple II-to-Pascal lineage is not documented here; record the immediate preserved Pascal source lineage. No independent build, gameplay or rights verification. Release 0.50 is explicitly titled Playable version; 0.60 publishes a 48 KiB cartridge and concrete gameplay fixes. Positive fields are bounded upstream evidence. Original assets and translated source rights were not independently established. No independent compilation, execution, gameplay, hardware or byte-exact verification was performed. title: Test Drive — DOS and Amiga native SDL3 reconstruction
reason: DOS EGA/CGA/Hercules and separately reconstructed Amiga versions share a coherent SDL3 port repository. Real-mode or 68000 memory layouts are retained as data, while gameplay is native C. Original EXE/ADF assets remain required. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; build/playability claims are upstream reports, not independent execution. title: Yawi — native SG-1000 / SC-3000 Enigma remake
reason: Substantial native C gameplay has levels, movement, tile collisions, gold and teleport handling; SDCC -mz80 script links SGlib/PSGlib and emits .sg/.sc ROMs. Release describes Enigma-inspired Boulderdash/Sokoban/XOR game with keyboard and pad. No independent build/run. Published release guarantees only first two of twelve levels; cut levels and missing elements may prevent later completion. Script references external crt0 components. No guest game-CPU interpreter path. SMS Power publishes a playable SG release and original code. Only the first two of twelve levels are stated completable; absent mechanics may block others. Source rebuild was not repeated and its external crt0 setup is not fully established.

title: ACEBasicJS — browser compiler and Amiga-inspired runtime
reason: New recursive-descent ACE BASIC-to-JavaScript compiler with browser runtime for Amiga-inspired screens/windows, input, graphics, sound, menus and turtle commands. Compiler explicitly treats C ACE as a reference specification; it emits JavaScript and does not emulate Amiga hardware. Source and static-server instructions are present. Compatibility is incremental and tied to documented seed programs, not full ACE/AmigaOS equivalence. No standalone license file was found in this repository; original ACE licensing should not automatically be copied to the new implementation.

title: CAMD I2C — native Amiga MIDI transmit driver
reason: camd-i2c.c implements CAMD callback handling and SendI2C at default address 0x42; main.c defines the resident driver entry points. CMake builds a freestanding driver with -m68040 and fetches i2c.library through CPM. Hardware and i2c.library are required; no particular attached MIDI device or working hardware configuration was independently verified. The inspected implementation establishes transmit functionality, not a complete bidirectional MIDI hardware stack. Bundled source is small but concrete; it is not a generic Amiga keyword-only hit.

title: Copper64 — C64 raster-list and interrupt library
reason: Implements programmable raster-line handler lists using VIC-II interrupts, inspired by the Amiga Copper idea. Native assembly provides color, video-mode, memory-bank, scrolling and custom-subroutine handlers; examples generate C64 PRGs. Amiga is conceptual inspiration only, so it is not added as a source or target platform. Many documented handlers are cycled for PAL 63-cycle lines. NTSC-specific support exists, but universal timing or hardware compatibility was not verified; example SID/music rights require separate care.

title: ILBMToIcon — Amiga icon-format converter
reason: ilbmtoicon.c contains concrete IFF ILBM/ByteRun1/chunk and icon serialization logic with libpng/zlib dependencies. README distinguishes old-style/pre3.5 image data, appended IFF ICON data and PNG icon output. Makefile uses HOST_CC; CMake also advertises m68k-amigaos packaging and builds infoinfo as companion utility. Output icon format and development target are Amiga; portable host build is not a claim of execution on every OS. No independent format compatibility or icon rendering test; input artwork rights remain the user’s responsibility.

title: Pinball Illusions — browser reconstruction
reason: Independent TypeScript browser reconstruction of the 1995 four-disk Amiga AGA release, with N-ball fixed-point simulation, collision maps, table mission-bytecode interpreter, canvas rendering and audio. Inspected ball-physics.ts and package.json show real implementation and Node/TypeScript build/test scripts; no 68k runtime wrapper is required. Original AGA release has three tables in this project; PC/console-exclusive Vikings is intentionally excluded. Inspected mode-vm.ts explicitly leaves eight mission opcodes unimplemented and deliberately ends missions when the ball ends, diverging from original behavior. This is not full gameplay parity. Upstream gameplay/parity/test counts are not independently validated and README explicitly retains contact-frame physics and sprite/collision alignment discrepancies. Ships disk-derived artwork, audio, music, geometry and mission data. Build rights gate requires PINBALL_ILLUSIONS_DERIVED_AUTHORIZED=1; this operator assertion is not evidence of redistribution permission. No repository license found. Re-extraction needs operator-owned original disks; clean-room description is upstream wording, not a legal conclusion.

title: Poseidon USB — standalone AmigaOS3 source restoration
reason: Main library source contains the full USB stack implementation; OS3 class_startup.c provides resident startup/open/close/expunge glue. upstream/aros.json pins the imported AROS commit and relocation map; src/LEGAL records Hodges’s 2009 AROS Public License release. Makefile builds OS3 library, class modules, GUI/tools and release packaging from source; components stay one stack candidate. Upstream explicitly says linked OS3 binaries still need real runtime validation, despite build checks. AROS hardware-controller code is retained but not staged for OS3; old closed E3B drivers, PsdLoadModule/PsdRestart and other unreleased pieces are absent. A complete compatible USB setup remains required; this is not a tested drop-in complete historical release.

title: ReFlood — native reconstruction of Amiga Flood
reason: C99/SDL2 native source reconstruction of Flood with game logic, asset extractor, audio/presentation, editor, deterministic test harness and experimental local split-screen mode. CMake defines a reusable flood_core and reflood/editor targets; src/game.c implements native gameplay rather than invoking an Amiga emulator. Only supported original IPF revision can be converted via disk-analyse and extracted; manifest checks reconstructed files. Original Flood data is not distributed in releases and is required for play and gameplay tests. Needs a legally obtained supported IPF plus disk-analyse with SPS/CAPS support. GPL-3.0 covers repository code; it does not license original assets. Multiplayer is experimental, editor cannot yet create/edit triggers. Latest editor-focus report explicitly lacks an XFCE/SDL runtime check. We did not build or run the game or editor.

title: rtl8139re.device — AmigaOS 4 driver reconstruction
reason: Repository describes reverse-engineered C reconstruction of Hyperion rtl8139.device; native SANA-II resident driver implements PCI enumeration, transmit handling and now IRQ/RX infrastructure. Makefile cross-compiles ppc-amigaos-gcc with -mcpu=440; target is AmigaOS 4 on QEMU sam460ex, with real Sam460ex/AmigaOne hardware only expected. Latest history documents Roadshow packet/copy-hook debugging and an RX rollback, so README pending-status table is stale relative to source. Incomplete driver: latest commit rolls back RX-side CallHookPkt dispatch; no claim of working full TCP/IP or production readiness. License explicitly TBD. Real-hardware compatibility is unverified; QEMU reports are upstream-only. PPC build flags identify target ISA, not 68k Amiga compatibility or minimum RAM.
